01The Premise

Most cars only look the part.

A splitter, a wing, a louder exhaust. The silhouette is easy to buy. The boundary is not.

Where, exactly, does a road car stop being a road car?

合法公路车的边界在哪？

Vol.7 opens with cars that wear the costume — and asks the uncomfortable question underneath it: if the bodywork can be bought, what actually makes a race car?

The answer is not in the silhouette. It is in the parts you cannot see: the structure that carries the load, the aerodynamics that only exist at speed, and the rules the car has to survive before it is allowed on the road.

The film calls it a boundary. The build treats it as a design constraint.

A / 01SilhouetteEasy to copy. A body kit is a purchase, not a proof.
A / 02StructureHard to fake. Load paths, aero surfaces, a floor that works.
A / 03LegalityImpossible to ignore. Every road rule is a performance tax.
Fig. 02 — Road equipment, in place

02The Car

天行健

TIAN XING JIAN

“As the heavens move, the machine endures.”

Built from a race car. Then made legal.

The starting point is the GSX EVO 9 — the car that set the lap in Vol.4. For Vol.7 it is rebuilt around a different constraint: it has to pass as a road car, not just a track weapon.

Road equipment is not decoration. Lights, mirrors, plates, clearance: every one is a concession, and every concession is a chance to lose performance. The build is the argument between the two.

02.1Object study

The details carry the argument.

Shot as objects, not trophies. These are the parts that have to survive a lap and a commute — and look deliberate doing both.

02.2Design

Nothing here is decorative.

Every vent feeds something. Every surface manages pressure. The body is not a costume — it is the first component of the aero map.

03Aerodynamics

1,400KG
Downforce at 250 km/h

Not a wing bolted on.

At 250 km/h the underbody generates 1,400 kilograms of downforce. The number comes from the floor, not the rear wing: Venturi tunnels accelerate the air beneath the car, drop its pressure, and pull the car into the road.

Active suspension keeps the platform where the aero map was drawn. As speed and load change, ride height changes with them — because downforce that stalls is just drag.

03.1+

Venturi tunnels

Full-length floor, fed by the front splitter. Pressure drop does the work a wing cannot do alone.

03.2+

Active suspension

Ride height managed in real time, keeping the floor in the window its aero map was drawn for.

03.3+

3 G lateral

Cornering load recorded in the episode. Downforce you can feel through the wheel, not just the graph.

04Powertrain

1,350 PS. A curve that behaves.

The headline is the number. The point is how early, and how evenly, it arrives.

The race engine made 1,963.5 PS. The road car makes 1,350. That is not simply a detune; it is a different contract with the throttle. A CNC-machined intake and a recalibrated map flatten the torque curve so power arrives early, evenly and repeatably.

Behind it, a 7-speed dual-clutch gearbox. No compromise on shift time. No drama at low speed.

Vol.7 ends before the clock does. The car is road-legal, the downforce is measured, the sprint is done — but a build is not a time attack until the lap is on the board.
